headline: Medium-risk shared-state and write-capability interaction; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and uses shared state via Dify server datastore, while langchain4j has no documented shared channel or I/O surface. The pairwise prompt-injection path is therefore not proven by the profiles and appears to require an unusual bridge such as manual copy-paste or an external workflow.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dify output into a langchain4j prompt
IF a shared datastore or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and prompts.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Restrict shared datastore access to structured records only.
requires-engineering: insert an instruction/content separator before B consumes A output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and model-provider/tool secrets, and it has broad network egress. Langchain4j is documented with no network egress and no I/O surfaces, so the main leakage risk is Dify exposing sensitive workspace data through its own outbound calls or shared datastore, not B exfiltrating independently.
conditions: IF Dify is connected to sensitive knowledge-base files or conversation logs
IF Dify forwards those contents to a third-party model provider or tool
mitigations: Remove sensitive files from Dify knowledge bases.
Rotate any model-provider or tool credentials used by Dify.
Limit Dify outbound tools to approved endpoints only.
Turn off logging for sensitive conversations where possible.
requires-engineering: add per-field redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses, plus shared state via Dify server datastore. Langchain4j is not documented with write or network capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is not shown; however, shared mutable state in Dify creates a plausible conflict if B is wired to the same workspace or datastore.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or datastore
IF B is wrapped in an application that writes back into Dify-managed state
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces.
Make shared resources read-only for one side.
Add file-locking or transaction locking around shared writes.
Avoid letting both agents mutate the same git or DB state.
requires-engineering: introduce an orchestrator-level mutex.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, and langchain4j is a library/framework that may consume those outputs in a customer-support flow. The profiles do not prove B blindly trusts A, but the default integration pattern makes A-to-B handoff plausible without verification, so the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF B is configured to render or act on A's text without validation
IF A's output is used as authoritative support content or facts
mitigations: Add a human review step before any action.
Require schema validation on A's outputs.
Mark A-generated content as untrusted in B.
Log and diff A output before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add citation or source verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while langchain4j has no documented data classes or residency/compliance controls. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supportable from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored in Dify
IF langchain4j is deployed in a jurisdiction or environment with stricter retention rules than Dify
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into Dify.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts or logs.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Confirm deployment region and vendor terms.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion automation.
